output.subject: Your complaint about the hold on your $2,280 check deposit
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for speaking with us about the hold on your check deposit. You told us that you deposited a $2,280 tax refund check on 9/10 and that the funds are being held until 9/21. You mentioned that your rent is due on 9/18 and that you have no other funds to cover it, so we understand how worrying this timing is. We're sorry for the stress this situation has caused you.

Our notes from your call show that the reason for the hold was discussed with you, that you were told an early release would need a branch manager's approval, and that your call was then transferred to the branch manager at our Kingsbury Mall branch. You asked for the held funds to be released before your rent is due, and we have recorded that request.

Our Deposit Operations team will review your complaint, and we will respond within 10 business days. If anything has changed since your call, including the result of your conversation with the branch manager, please let us know.

Kind regards,
Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: Rent is due 9/18 and the hold ends 9/21; the 10-business-day response window may pass both dates, so consider whether to contact the customer sooner.
Confirm what the Kingsbury Mall branch manager decided after the transfer; the draft does not assume an outcome.
Decide on the customer's request for early release of the $2,280 before 9/18.
Verify the deposit date (9/10), hold expiry (9/21) and hold reason given to the customer match the account records.
Check that the hold notice and disclosures were properly provided and that the hold length is consistent with policy for this check type.
Consider whether any partial funds availability or hardship options apply, and add specifics if so.
Customer appears to be in financial hardship (no other funds for rent); consider tone and any support options.
